solution.name: Swap Space Solution
solution.description:
Implement solution.py that solves the Swap Space problem.

Algorithm:
1. Read n drives, each with old capacity a_i and new capacity b_i.
2. Determine the minimum extra storage E needed to reformat all drives.

Key insight: We need to find an optimal ordering of drives to reformat that minimizes the required extra space. The greedy strategy is:
- Split drives into two groups: those that grow (b_i >= a_i) and those that shrink (b_i < a_i).
- Reformat growing drives first (sorted by a_i ascending — evacuate cheapest first, gaining free space).
- Then reformat shrinking drives (sorted by b_i descending — the ones that lose the least capacity first).

Simulation: Track available free space. Start with free_space = E (the extra drive). For each drive in the chosen order, we need free_space >= a_i to evacuate it. After reformatting, free_space increases by b_i (the drive is now empty with new capacity, but data was moved to free space, so net change is b_i - a_i). We need to find the minimum E such that free_space never goes negative.

Direct computation (no binary search needed):
- Sort drives in the optimal order described above.
- Simulate with E = 0. Track free_space. When free_space < a_i, record the deficit.
- The answer is the maximum cumulative deficit encountered (i.e., the minimum E that makes all steps feasible).

More precisely: start with free = 0. For each drive in order: free -= a_i (evacuate data), if free < min_free update min_free, then free += b_i (reformatted drive available). Answer = -min_free if min_free < 0, else 0. But per constraints n >= 1, so answer >= 1... actually answer could be 0 if somehow possible, but we must evacuate at least the first drive so answer >= min(a_i) unless we have enough from new capacities. Wait — no, answer is max(0, -min_free).

Actually re-checking: the answer CAN be 0 only if you never need extra space, which is impossible since the first drive must be evacuated somewhere. So answer >= min(a_i) for the first drive... unless we account for free space from other sources. But initially there's only the extra drive. So answer >= a_i of the first reformatted drive, which is min(a_i) among growing drives (sorted by a_i asc). So answer > 0 always.

Implementation:
- Read input from stdin.
- Sort drives as described.
- Simulate and compute minimum extra space.
- Print result.

File: solution.py
Constraints: n up to 10^6, capacities up to 10^9. O(n log n) time due to sorting.

contract.name: Swap Space Solution
contract.description: Implement solution.py that solves the Swap Space problem. Given n drives with old capacities a_i and new capacities b_i, determine the minimum extra storage E needed to reformat all drives. Uses a greedy ordering strategy: reformat growing drives first (sorted by a_i ascending), then shrinking drives (sorted by b_i descending). Simulates free space tracking to compute the answer directly without binary search. Reads from stdin, writes to stdout. O(n log n) time, O(n) space, standard library only.

structured_side_effects.description: Pure parsing function with no side effects.

functions.name: solve
functions.description: Given a list of drives, compute the minimum extra storage E needed to reformat all drives. Strategy: split drives into growers (new_capacity >= old_capacity) and shrinkers (new_capacity < old_capacity). Sort growers by old_capacity ascending, shrinkers by new_capacity descending. Concatenate growers then shrinkers. Simulate free space: start free=0, min_free=0. For each drive: free -= old_capacity; min_free = min(min_free, free); free += new_capacity. Return max(0, -min_free).

inputs.name: drives
inputs.description: List of drives to reformat, each with old_capacity and new_capacity.

preconditions: All drives have old_capacity >= 1 and new_capacity >= 1.
postconditions: E is the minimum extra storage such that all drives can be reformatted in the computed optimal order without free space ever going negative.
Starting with free_space = E and processing drives in the optimal greedy order, free_space >= 0 at every step (after evacuating each drive).
No smaller non-negative integer E' < E satisfies the above property for any ordering of drives.

structured_side_effects.description: Pure computation with no side effects.

functions.name: main
functions.description: Entry point. Reads all input from stdin via sys.stdin.read(), parses it with parse_input, computes the answer with solve, and prints the single integer result to stdout followed by a newline.

error_cases.condition: Input from stdin does not conform to expected format, propagated from parse_input.

preconditions: stdin contains valid input conforming to the problem format.
Program is invoked as the main module.
postconditions: Exactly one line is written to stdout containing the integer result.
The printed integer is the minimum extra storage E needed to reformat all drives.
No other output is written to stdout or stderr.
side_effects: Reads from stdin (consumes entire stdin stream).

structured_side_effects.description: Reads entire contents of stdin via sys.stdin.read() for fast bulk I/O.
Prints the single integer answer followed by a newline to stdout via print().

invariants: The program uses only the Python 3.10+ standard library; no external dependencies.
All functions have complete type annotations.
The greedy ordering is: growers (b >= a) sorted by a ascending, then shrinkers (b < a) sorted by b descending.

The simulation computes the minimum extra space E by tracking the minimum free space encountered: E = max(0, -min_free) where min_free is the running minimum of cumulative (sum of b_i - a_i) over the prefix.
For n >= 1 with all capacities >= 1, the answer E >= min(a_i) of the first drive in the sorted order (since the first drive must be fully evacuated with no prior free space from other drives).
Time complexity is O(n log n) dominated by sorting; space complexity is O(n).
Output is exactly one line containing the integer E with no leading zeros (except E=0 itself), no trailing spaces, terminated by a newline.
The file contains an if __name__ == '__main__': main() guard.
